svg.title: Five kinds of latency
svg.desc: Five non-exclusive latency classes with one source-ledger example each, and a matrix of how often the ledger assigns two classes to the same case.
svg.text: The classes overlap: every case in the ledger carries two of them. Each example below is assigned to its class in the case ledger.
Information explicitly recorded but subsequently forgotten, inaccessible, or overlooked.
RB-018 · Vesuvius Challenge recovers text from sealed scroll scans
Meaningful connections among artifacts that have not been recognized or
RB-016 · Fish-oil and Raynaud literature joined before a clinical trial
Conclusions or hypotheses obtainable by combining observations, claims, or constraints.
RB-004 · Madoff return and options-volume red flags
Previously known information whose relevance becomes apparent under different
conditions or in a different domain.
RB-023 · House-allocation cycles adapted to kidney exchange
Structure or associations encoded in a computational representation, such as an embedding
or trained model, that require elicitation and independent verification.
RB-006 · Thermoelectric candidates from pre-cutoff word embeddings
Each cell counts the ledger cases that carry both classes. The
diagonal counts every case assigned to the class.
Most frequent pairing: Relational and Contextual, 9 cases.
Never paired in the ledger: Archival and Contextual;
Definitions are LIA's own, verbatim. Examples illustrate a class, not an exclusive taxonomy; the finance warning is an oversight case, not proof of previously unknown fraud.
Matrix counts are computed from the case ledger and are not frequencies in the world.
Sources: RB-018; RB-016; RB-004; RB-023; RB-006; RB case ledger
